pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of severe non-peritoneal abdominal pain, SIADH-induced hyponatremia, ascending motor neuropathy exacerbated by a CYP450 inducer (phenytoin), and urine turning dark port-wine colored upon light exposure. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD), an essential enzyme in the heme biosynthesis pathway. Caloric restriction (fasting) or administration of CYP450-inducing drugs (like phenytoin) dramatically upregulates hepatic delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase 1 (ALAS1). This enzymatic bottleneck leads to the catastrophic accumulation of neurotoxic heme precursors—specifically delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG)—triggering severe autonomic dysfunction, neuro-visceral attacks, psychosis, and peripheral neurotoxicity. PBG oxidizes to porphobilin and porphyrins when exposed to air and UV light, producing the classic port-wine coloration.
